You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From fb92647f50a3edcd0eedaa3bf2b6fa960fa199a0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: edoapra <edoardo.apra@gmail.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Jul 2018 12:47:28 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] fix for bug introduced in
 bc83ddd8eeb3f9cea459e1ef18c100205d39a858: set shell.screen_max to large value
 (not zero)

---
 skel/simint/shell/shell.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/skel/simint/shell/shell.c b/skel/simint/shell/shell.c
index 04bb28c..921aa34 100644
--- a/skel/simint/shell/shell.c
+++ b/skel/simint/shell/shell.c
@@ -431,7 +431,7 @@ void simint_fill_multi_shellpair2(int npair, struct simint_shell const * AB,
     P->nshell12 = npair;
     P->nshell12_clip = npair; // by default, it's the same
     P->nprim = 0;
-    P->screen_max = 0.0;
+    P->screen_max = 1.e99;
 
     // zero out
     // This is not really needed, and can be expensive in
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by setting the `screen_max` variable to zero, which likely led to incorrect behavior in the program. The patch corrects this by initializing `screen_max` to a very large value (1.e99) instead of zero, ensuring that the program can function correctly without being constrained by a zero value that could cause issues in calculations or logic that depend on this variable.
